text:
Matt Coronato has 15 points in 18 games, which looks like the same productive young winger Calgary has been building around. Look closer and the season splits in two. Eleven of the points are assists, seven came on the power play, and his own chances have thinned out: 1.6 expected goals over his last ten games, well under his usual rate, and only 4 goals all year.

At five on five the Flames get just 42% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, yet they have scored 5 more goals than those chances deserve. That is the cushion under his point total, and on-ice luck like that rarely lasts.

There is good news in the profile. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 8.5 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area last season, 98th percentile, which is exactly the kind of shooter who should be scoring more than 4 goals. Our projection is about 57 points. We'd bet on the goals coming before the luck runs out, but the defensive numbers need to improve too.
headline: Coronato's points are running ahead of his play
